utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice. I don't think that you're going to finish with your direct-examination this evening. If you prefer that I speak directly to Witness K. Perhaps it would be better to stop at ten to six, in another ten minutes, which would allow you to rest at your hotel, and perhaps that would be better.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All right. We're going to go for about another ten minutes and then we're going to stop and resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While it's being circulated, I imagine that the Chamber and my friend will have no difficulty following the sketch because of its familiarity with the hangars which are shown on the right and the office buildings which are shown more divided up into smaller units on the left. Could it be placed on the ELMO? Could the jug of water be moved? I suspect it might be in the way, and if the pointer could be extended. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, this is a plan. You drew this yourself, I think, didn't you, at one stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As I just suggested to the Judges, the hangar is on the right as we can see it, and the offices are on the left, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, you've been in the offices, and you were then taken or ordered out. Where did you go when you were taken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: They took me out. It was dark. It was a lot soldier and policemen, and for moment I -- I lost, disappear my vision from another my co-worker, someone, other person pushing me toward the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: They guide me toward the wall, actually, next to the -- yes. They told me to turn toward the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, when you did that, did you notice some detainees, some prisoners near you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: When I walking I saw the line, a line of the people, maybe around -- it was dark. I saw body, like, you know, between -- not too dark and I saw the bodies, and it was maybe around 50 people all the line, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were they all in one line or was there more than one row of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: One line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: And I was first, next to door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: These men, what were they doing? Where were their hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: On top, on the wall. You know, hold up to the wall. Leaning against the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you hear anything said at about this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yeah. Behind our back I will heard you know, the people, like running, putting -- standing in the back behind the line, you know, and sound of machine, you know, when they -- and a lot steps, you know, walking behind our back. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you hear anything said or anything shouted, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes. When they say to, you know, like get prepare or get ready, and I turned my head toward to them accidentally, and some of them, they told me, you know, "Get out." But I didn't know they talked to me until they come close to me, actually one soldier, and said, "Go with me." During the walking they will -- they will walk. The soldier was in the line, you know, my shoulder, you know, in the line, yes. He will guide me to the same office where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you hear something else? You heard --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You'd heard the shout --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: When I was walking, during the walking I shout -- I heard, you know -- you know, like ready, shooting, you know, a lot guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You heard the word "ready." Did you hear any other instruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Like shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then the sound you heard after that was the sound of what, guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Sound of the gun, a lot sound of the gun, and sounds like, you know, like the body falling down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You came back across to the offices. Did you go into the offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes. I will walk. I could not turn because the guard was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: And he will guide me in the same room where I was previous, and he will brought me the room, and I didn't even sit. I will hear the voice again previous, crazy, crazy guy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's the man who had been in the office and made you all assault each other; is that right? Tried to make you assault each other.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What did he do to you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: He put me in the chair. Put me in the chair. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: He will sit in the front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could stop at this point, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the summary, these are very difficult things to say. Since we've only taken one break this afternoon and everybody needs to rest -- Witness K, we're going to interrupt a little earlier than we expected to. With the assistance of the person with you, you're going to go to the Victims and Witnesses Section and try to rest. I'm sure this has been -- tomorrow morning will be difficult, so try to rest this evening. You were very courageous. All right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do not move. The Judges are going to withdraw, and we will see one another again tomorrow at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: at 5.50 p.m. to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of September, 1999 at 10.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
